dimension-tabs.title: Dimension tabs
dimension-tabs.text: These tabs change the whole explorer. State shows a US tile map; other dimensions show one tile per segment. Every tab uses the same primary mature test window: {primary_window}, {n_oot} resolved loans.
dimension-tabs.try: Switch to Grade, then click the tile with the highest expected loss.

metric-tabs.title: Color metric
metric-tabs.text: The color metric decides how tiles and bars are ordered and colored. Observed default is what actually happened; predicted PD is the model's calibrated estimate; expected loss combines PD, LGD and EAD.
metric-tabs.try: Choose Predicted PD and compare the ranking with observed default.

map.title: Segment map
map.text: Each tile is one segment. Hover or focus a tile to see loans, the observed default rate with a 95% Wilson interval, predicted PD and expected loss. Tiles with fewer than {min_n} loans are hatched and marked with an exclamation point because their rates are too noisy to rank.
map.try: Select California and compare its 95% interval with a small state.

ranked-list.title: Ranked segments
ranked-list.text: This list sorts the same segments by the selected metric. Longer bars mean a higher value on that metric. A row and its map tile stay linked, so clicking either one selects the same segment.
ranked-list.try: Click the top row, then use the browser Back button.

filter.title: Filter segments
filter.text: Type part of a state, grade, purpose, vintage, term or home-ownership label. The filter only hides rows; it does not change the selected segment or the portfolio totals.
filter.try: Type CA, then clear the box.

kpi-loans.title: Resolved loans (2007–2018)
kpi-loans.text: This is the full analysis sample: {n_rows} loans with a final outcome anywhere in the 2007–2018 snapshot. It is not the same as the primary test window.
kpi-loans.try: Compare it with the {n_oot} loans in the explorer below.

kpi-observed.title: Observed default rate
kpi-observed.text: The share of loans in the segment that ended as Charged Off or Default. This is a descriptive historical rate, not a causal effect and not a forecast.
kpi-observed.try: Select a segment and compare its rate with the portfolio rate of {default_rate_oot}.

kpi-ci.title: 95% confidence interval
kpi-ci.text: The Wilson interval shows the sampling uncertainty around the observed default rate. A small segment can have a wide interval even when its point estimate looks dramatic.
kpi-ci.try: Hover a state with fewer than {min_n} loans and compare its interval width.

kpi-pd.title: Predicted PD
kpi-pd.text: The mean calibrated probability of default for the segment. It is a model output on the mature test window, not the observed default rate; the two can differ.
kpi-pd.try: Switch between Observed default and Predicted PD and watch the ranking move.

kpi-el.title: Expected loss % of EAD
kpi-el.text: Expected loss is PD × LGD, expressed as a share of exposure. It turns a probability into an average loss estimate. The portfolio total is reconciled to the headline EL rate of {el_rate}.
kpi-el.try: Compare the selected segment with the portfolio total.

kpi-ead.title: EAD share
kpi-ead.text: Exposure at default is the loan amount at risk. EAD share shows how much of the portfolio's exposure sits in this segment; a high default rate in a tiny segment may matter less than a small rate in a large one.
kpi-ead.try: Find the segment with the largest EAD share.

score-distribution.title: Score distribution
score-distribution.text: The bars count test-window loans by scorecard score for the selected segment. Higher scores mean lower risk. The shape matters: two segments with the same average can have very different tails.
score-distribution.try: Compare the distribution of a high-loss grade with the portfolio.

risk-rho.title: Asset correlation (ρ)
risk-rho.text: ρ controls how much loans move together through the systematic factor. A higher ρ makes defaults cluster in bad years and pushes the tail of the loss distribution up. The slider snaps to a precomputed grid.
risk-rho.try: Drag ρ from its base case toward the right and watch VaR 99.9%.

risk-pd.title: PD stress
risk-pd.text: This multiplies every loan's probability of default by the chosen factor before simulation. It answers “what if defaults are more frequent than the calibrated baseline?” It is a stress, not a forecast.
risk-pd.try: Set PD stress to a higher multiplier and compare ES 99.9%.

risk-lgd.title: LGD stress
risk-lgd.text: This multiplies loss given default before simulation. It asks what happens if recoveries are worse than the portfolio-level assumption. PD stress and LGD stress can be combined.
risk-lgd.try: Raise both PD and LGD stress and watch the loss histogram shift right.

play-rho.title: Play the rho sweep
play-rho.text: The sweep moves ρ through the precomputed grid so you can see the tail respond. It does not re-simulate in the browser. With reduced motion enabled it advances one step per activation instead of animating.
play-rho.try: Start the sweep, then pause it on a high-ρ point.

risk-el.title: Expected loss in the simulation
risk-el.text: The average loss across simulated paths. It should sit near the headline expected loss; small differences come from the finite number of paths and the scenario grid.
risk-el.try: Compare this with the headline EL of {el_rate}.

risk-ul.title: Unexpected loss
risk-ul.text: The standard deviation of simulated losses around expected loss. It measures how much the loss typically varies, before looking at the extreme tail.
risk-ul.try: Increase PD stress and watch UL rise.

risk-var99.title: VaR 99%
risk-var99.text: In 99 of 100 simulated years, the portfolio loss stays below this share of EAD. It is a quantile of the simulated loss distribution, not a maximum possible loss.

risk-var999.title: VaR 99.9%
risk-var999.text: In 999 of 1,000 simulated years, the portfolio loss stays below this share of EAD. It is more sensitive to the tail and to asset correlation than VaR 99%.
risk-var999.try: Move ρ and watch how much more VaR 99.9% changes than VaR 99%.

risk-es99.title: Expected Shortfall 99%
risk-es99.text: The average loss in the worst 1% of simulated years. Unlike VaR, ES averages the tail instead of stopping at one quantile.

risk-es999.title: Expected Shortfall 99.9%
risk-es999.text: The average loss in the worst 0.1% of simulated years. This is the most tail-sensitive number in the Risk Lab.
risk-es999.try: Raise ρ and PD stress together and watch ES 99.9%.

gauge.title: VaR gauge
gauge.text: The gauge places VaR 99.9% on a 0–60% loss scale so the current scenario has a visual reference. The scale is descriptive; it is not a regulatory limit or an appetite statement.
gauge.try: Use the surface to pick a high-stress point and watch the needle.

loss-histogram.title: Loss distribution
loss-histogram.text: Each bar counts simulated portfolio losses for the current scenario. The vertical lines mark EL, VaR 99%, VaR 99.9% and ES 99%; the legend lists their values so the labels never collide.
loss-histogram.try: Increase LGD stress and see how far the whole distribution moves right.

surface.title: VaR surface
surface.text: The surface shows the selected risk metric across ρ and PD stress on the precomputed grid. The dark marker is the current scenario and the outlined marker is the base case. Click or tap a point to move the sliders.
surface.try: Click a high-ρ, high-PD point and then read the histogram.

surface-metric.title: Surface metric
surface-metric.text: Switch the vertical axis between VaR 99.9%, ES 99.9% and expected loss. The surface uses the same simulation grid, so only the displayed metric changes.
surface-metric.try: Compare the shape of EL with the shape of ES 99.9%.

sim-annual_inc.title: Annual income
sim-annual_inc.text: Gross yearly income reported at application. In the scorecard, higher income generally earns more points because it is associated with lower observed risk.
sim-annual_inc.try: Choose the typical preset, then lower income one bin.

sim-dti.title: Debt-to-income ratio
sim-dti.text: Monthly debt payments divided by monthly income. Higher DTI means less room for a new payment; the scorecard contribution reflects that relationship.
sim-dti.try: Move DTI up and watch the point contribution change.

sim-revol_util.title: Credit card utilization
sim-revol_util.text: The share of available revolving credit currently used. High utilization is associated with higher observed risk in this project.
sim-revol_util.try: Compare low and high utilization presets.

sim-inq_last_6mths.title: Credit inquiries
sim-inq_last_6mths.text: How many lenders checked the applicant's credit in the last six months. More inquiries are associated with higher risk here.
sim-inq_last_6mths.try: Set inquiries to the highest bin and read the score.

sim-home_ownership.title: Home ownership
sim-home_ownership.text: Whether the applicant rents, owns, or has a mortgage. Categories are ordered by frequency in the test window; the score impact comes from the published points table.

sim-purpose.title: Loan purpose
sim-purpose.text: The reason the borrower gave for the loan. Categories are grouped into the published scorecard bins, with rare categories combined under “Other / rare categories.”
sim-purpose.try: Compare Debt consolidation with Credit card.

sim-installment_to_income.title: Monthly payment vs income
sim-installment_to_income.text: The monthly loan payment as a share of monthly income. The project computes it as installment × 12 ÷ annual income, which is the same ratio on a monthly basis.
sim-installment_to_income.try: Raise the payment share and watch the score fall.

sim-score.title: Score
sim-score.text: The score adds a fixed base to the points for each selected bin. Higher score means lower implied risk. The breakdown below the result lists every contribution.
sim-score.try: Open “Why this score?” and check the arithmetic.

sim-pd.title: Implied PD
sim-pd.text: The score is mapped to a probability of default through the published scorecard scaling. The text also translates it into “about N out of 100 similar applicants” and compares it with the portfolio default rate of {default_rate_oot}.
sim-pd.try: Compare the typical and higher-risk presets.

sim-percentile.title: Percentile
sim-percentile.text: This says how many test-window loans have a lower score. It is phrased as “scores higher than X%” so the direction is unambiguous: a higher percentile is better.
sim-percentile.try: Move one input and watch the percentile shift.

sim-breakdown.title: Why this score?
sim-breakdown.text: The breakdown lists the fixed base points and each variable's contribution. The base plus every contribution equals the displayed score, so the arithmetic is auditable.
sim-breakdown.try: Change one input and confirm that only its row moves.

sim-presets.title: Applicant presets
sim-presets.text: Typical picks the most common test-window bin for each variable. Lower-risk picks the highest-points bin; higher-risk picks the lowest-points bin; Reset returns to Typical.
sim-presets.try: Load Lower-risk, then Higher-risk, and compare the PD.

cutoff-slider.title: Score cutoff
cutoff-slider.text: Applicants at or above this score are approved. Moving the cutoff trades approval volume against the bad rate among approved loans. The published KS cutoff is marked separately.
cutoff-slider.try: Find the approximate cutoff where the bad rate rises sharply.

cutoff-approval.title: Approval rate
cutoff-approval.text: The share of test-window loans that would be approved at this cutoff. It is a historical what-if, not a business decision.

cutoff-bad.title: Bad rate (approved)
cutoff-bad.text: The default rate among approved loans at this cutoff. A higher cutoff usually lowers this number but also rejects more good borrowers.
cutoff-bad.try: Compare it with the overall default rate.

cutoff-approved-good.title: Approved good loans
cutoff-approved-good.text: Loans that would be approved and did not default. This is the good volume retained by the cutoff.
cutoff-approved-good.try: Raise the cutoff and watch this count fall.

cutoff-approved-bad.title: Approved bad loans
cutoff-approved-bad.text: Loans that would be approved and did default. These are the false negatives of the approval rule from the lender's perspective.
cutoff-approved-bad.try: Lower the cutoff and watch this count rise.

theme-toggle.title: Theme
theme-toggle.text: Cycles Auto, Light and Dark. Auto follows the operating system. The choice is stored in the URL hash so a shared link keeps the same appearance.
theme-toggle.try: Switch to Dark and reload the page.

provenance.title: How do we know?
provenance.text: Opens the provenance drawer: data source, window, sample size, formulas, small-n masking and the limitations that remain. It is the audit trail for the numbers on screen.
provenance.try: Read the limitations before quoting a segment.
